lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68 — translate only lazy-loads config.locale; fallback locales are loaded solely in ApplicationController#set_locale, so jobs/mailers/rake/specs silently skip fallbacks and the resulting "translation missing" string is cached and keeps being served after the fallbacks load

config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — FallbackLocaleList#[] overrides Hash#[] without memoizing, so every backend translate (all interpolated I18n.t calls and every LRU miss) allocates three arrays and reads SiteSetting.default_locale, where stock I18n::Locale::Fallbacks caches the chain per locale.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:69 — Interpolated I18n.t calls skip the LRU cache, so for partially translated user locales each miss now tries up to 3 locales and allocates and throws a MissingTranslation per locale on every call, with no caching.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — LRU cache key omits the fallback chain (SiteSetting.default_locale), so in multisite a fallback string cached for one site is served to other sites with a different default locale, and results cached before fallback locales loaded (e.g. "translation missing") stay stale for the life of the process.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:21 — Fallback locales are only loaded by ApplicationController#set_locale; Sidekiq jobs, mailers, and rake tasks (and I18n.t with an explicit locale: option) never call ensure_loaded!, and translate only lazy-loads config.locale, so fallbacks to the site default locale or en return "translation missing" there.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — New FallbackLocaleList chain (user locale -> site default -> en, dedup when user locale == default) ships with no spec covering any fallback resolution case.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — LRU cache key omits SiteSetting.default_locale/fallback chain, so a runtime default_locale change serves stale fallback strings, and no test covers cache invalidation.

app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 — Fallback locales are only preloaded in set_locale, so jobs/mailers/non-controller translate calls have their fallback locales unloaded and silently get no fallback, with no test covering these paths.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:24 — Fallbacks moved from production-only config into a global initializer, so test/dev now mask missing translations, and no spec asserts missing-key behavior under the new setup.
lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:69 — The interpolation path (translate_no_cache with args) combined with fallbacks has no test for falling back while interpolating.
lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62 — New I18n.ensure_loaded! helper, including its lazy @loaded_locales init, has no unit test.

goldens.comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — LRU cache key is only key+locale+backend, but fallback results now depend on per-site SiteSetting.default_locale, so a default_locale change (or another multisite site with a different default) gets stale cross-site fallback strings

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds custom I18n fallbacks that depend on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`) and adds `ensure_loaded!` to the translate accelerator, but it does not show any LRU cache implementation or cache key composition (e.g., key+locale+backend) at or around the cited line. Without the cache code in the diff, the claim about stale cross-site fallback strings due to an insufficient cache key cannot be verified from what’s changed here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68 — translate only lazy-loads config.locale; fallback locales are loaded solely in ApplicationController#set_locale, so jobs/mailers/rake/specs silently skip fallbacks and the resulting "translation missing" string is cached and keeps being served after the fallbacks load

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds lazy-loading in `TranslateAccelerator#translate` that only loads `config.locale` (`load_locale(config.locale) unless ...`), and introduces fallback-locale preloading via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` which is only invoked in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. The new `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` explicitly loads `I18n.locale` plus fallback locales (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`) by calling `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each, but nothing in the diff ensures this runs for non-controller execution paths (jobs/mailers/rake/specs). Therefore, fallback locales may not be loaded when translations are first looked up outside controllers, leading to missing translations despite fallbacks being configured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — FallbackLocaleList#[] overrides Hash#[] without memoizing, so every backend translate (all interpolated I18n.t calls and every LRU miss) allocates three arrays and reads SiteSetting.default_locale, where stock I18n::Locale::Fallbacks caches the chain per locale.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb` and overrides `#[]` to return `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`, which allocates a new array and reads `SiteSetting.default_locale` on every call. There is no memoization/caching in this override (despite inheriting from `Hash`), so repeated fallback-chain lookups will repeatedly allocate and recompute. This is a performance/efficiency concern rather than a correctness defect, and it is grounded directly in the new `#[]` implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:69 — Interpolated I18n.t calls skip the LRU cache, so for partially translated user locales each miss now tries up to 3 locales and allocates and throws a MissingTranslation per locale on every call, with no caching.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a custom fallback chain of up to three locales (`FallbackLocaleList#[]` returns `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`) and ensures fallback locales are loaded per request (`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`). In `TranslateAccelerator#translate`, interpolated calls still bypass the cache (`return translate_no_cache(key, *args) if args.length > 0`, shown in the diff context). With fallbacks now enabled via `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` and `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`, missing keys in partially translated locales will plausibly cause additional per-call lookup work across multiple locales for interpolated translations without benefiting from the existing cache. The specific claim about allocating/throwing `MissingTranslation` objects isn’t directly verifiable from the diff, but the cache-bypass + added fallback chain performance concern is grounded in the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — LRU cache key omits the fallback chain (SiteSetting.default_locale), so in multisite a fallback string cached for one site is served to other sites with a different default locale, and results cached before fallback locales loaded (e.g. "translation missing") stay stale for the life of the process.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show any LRU cache key construction or how cached translation results are keyed, so the claim that the key “omits the fallback chain (SiteSetting.default_locale)” is not verifiable from the provided changes. The diff instead adds `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `set_locale` and adds `TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded!`, which appear intended to avoid stale lookups due to unloaded fallback locales, contradicting the finding’s “translation missing stays stale” assertion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:21 — Fallback locales are only loaded by ApplicationController#set_locale; Sidekiq jobs, mailers, and rake tasks (and I18n.t with an explicit locale: option) never call ensure_loaded!, and translate only lazy-loads config.locale, so fallbacks to the site default locale or en return "translation missing" there.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a custom `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` (config/initializers/i18n.rb) that explicitly loads fallback locales via `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, but the only new call site is `ApplicationController#set_locale` (`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`). Meanwhile `TranslateAccelerator#translate` still lazy-loads only `config.locale`, not the fallback locales, and nothing in the diff shows `ensure_loaded!` being invoked in non-controller contexts (jobs, mailers, rake tasks). That makes it plausible that fallback lookups (to `SiteSetting.default_locale` or `:en`) can return `translation missing` in those contexts because the fallback locales’ translations were never loaded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] on every lookup, so every I18n.t now depends on SiteSetting.default_locale; any translation during boot, migrations, or asset precompile when SiteSetting cannot load or refresh (DB down, no table) raises instead of translating.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `FallbackLocaleList#[]` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb` which computes fallbacks as `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`. That makes fallback resolution depend on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (and thus whatever `SiteSetting` needs, potentially DB-backed) at runtime. However, the claim that `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` "on every lookup" and that this will definitively raise during boot/migrations/precompile cannot be verified from this diff alone (it depends on I18n internals and SiteSetting behavior). It is a concrete, diff-grounded risk/architecture issue rather than a provable defect from the patch itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — New FallbackLocaleList chain (user locale -> site default -> en, dedup when user locale == default) ships with no spec covering any fallback resolution case.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new, nontrivial fallback behavior via `FallbackLocaleList#[]` and `#ensure_loaded!` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb` (custom chain `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`), and wires it into runtime via `I18n.fallbacks = ...` plus `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. No corresponding test/spec changes are shown in the diff to exercise fallback resolution or the dedup/ordering behavior. While the diff alone can’t prove there are zero existing specs elsewhere, it does show new logic landing without any added coverage alongside it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — LRU cache key omits SiteSetting.default_locale/fallback chain, so a runtime default_locale change serves stale fallback strings, and no test covers cache invalidation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a custom I18n fallback list (config/initializers/i18n.rb) and an `ensure_loaded!` helper in `translate_accelerator`, but it does not show any LRU cache key construction or how cached translations are keyed. Without seeing the caching logic at/around the referenced line, the claim that the cache key omits `SiteSetting.default_locale`/fallback chain (and thus serves stale fallback strings after a runtime change) is not directly verifiable from this diff. The statement about missing tests is also not provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 — Fallback locales are only preloaded in set_locale, so jobs/mailers/non-controller translate calls have their fallback locales unloaded and silently get no fallback, with no test covering these paths.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces explicit fallback-locale preloading via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale` (app/controllers/application_controller.rb), and a custom `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` that calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each fallback (config/initializers/i18n.rb). No other entrypoint (e.g., jobs/mailers) is shown calling this new preloading hook, so non-controller translation paths may not benefit from the same eager loading behavior. However, the claim that they will “silently get no fallback” isn’t directly provable from the diff alone because fallback lookups might still trigger lazy loading depending on how `TranslateAccelerator` and the I18n backend interact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:24 — Fallbacks moved from production-only config into a global initializer, so test/dev now mask missing translations, and no spec asserts missing-key behavior under the new setup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from production/profile (and cloud66 production) and instead globally enables fallbacks via `config/initializers/i18n.rb` (`require 'i18n/backend/fallbacks'`, include `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks`, and `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`). Initializers run in all environments, so this change does expand fallback behavior beyond production. The claim about “no spec asserts missing-key behavior” is not verifiable from this diff alone (no tests are shown/modified), but the environment-scope change is real and review-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:69 — The interpolation path (translate_no_cache with args) combined with fallbacks has no test for falling back while interpolating.

adjudication.rationale: The finding asserts a lack of tests (“has no test for falling back while interpolating”), but the provided diff shows only production code changes (initializers/controller/translate_accelerator) and no test suite context. From this diff alone we cannot verify whether such a test exists elsewhere or is missing. The diff does show an interpolation path (`translate` returning `translate_no_cache` when `args.length > 0`) and newly added fallbacks setup, but the claim specifically about test coverage is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62 — New I18n.ensure_loaded! helper, including its lazy @loaded_locales init, has no unit test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` (`def ensure_loaded!(locale)` with lazy `@loaded_locales ||= []` and conditional `load_locale`) and wires it into request flow via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale` and `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` calling `I18n.ensure_loaded!`. No test additions/changes are shown in the diff to cover this new lazy-loading helper and its caching semantics, which is a specific, nontrivial logic change worth testing, though the absence of tests cannot be proven solely from the provided diff.
